title: Front-running the Goldman roll (Mou 2011) on 2010-2026 CME data (entirely after the paper's sample)
registered: 2026-10-20, from the user-supplied paper, before any Gen129 number
paper: Mou (2011), 'Limits to Arbitrage and Commodity Index Investment: Front-Running the Goldman Roll'. The S&P GSCI rolls from the 5th to the 9th business day of each month. Strategy 1 enters a calendar spread 10 business days before the roll (short the contract being rolled out of, long the one rolled into) and unwinds over the roll; Strategy 2 enters 5 business days before. 2000-2010 Sharpe up to 4.39; energy was the best sector; profits fell as arbitrage capital grew after 2004
implementation: for each commodity, the two contracts are the volume-ranked front and second Databento contracts, ordered by listing date (near/far). Spread return = -(near/far at exit / near/far at entry - 1) (short near, long far, equal notional). A month is traded only if the SAME pair of contracts is held at entry and every exit. Exit = average of the unwinds at the closes of business days 5..9 (20% each). Costs: 2 legs x (1 tick + commission) in and out

tests.R1 Strategy 1, energy (CL HO RB NG), PRI: enter at the close 10 business days before business day 5 of the month; equal weight across the commodities traded that month; 1x notional per spread
tests.R2 Strategy 2, energy: enter 5 business days before business day 5

rule: DEV 2010-17 > 0, TEST 2018-22 >= 0.5, HOLD 2023-26 >= 0.3 (daily P&L, Sharpe on business days)
caveat: the paper reports decay as arbitrageurs entered; our whole sample is post-2010, so this is a strict out-of-sample test
